query: Equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr has 8–16% room-temperature tensile ductility in the cast state and a yield strength of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C at strain rates of 10−4–10−2 s−1, but its poor oxygen resistance limits practical high-temperature use. What single intervention could overcome this limitation without sacrificing the alloy’s useful mechanical performance? Formulate one hypothesis specifying the intervention and mechanism, the predicted change relative to untreated cast HfNbTaTiZr, the relevant temperature, atmosphere, exposure time, and mechanical-loading boundaries, supporting prior evidence, and a controlled falsification experiment.

generation.hypothesis: Applying a thin, adherent aluminide coating that forms a stable alumina scale will improve the oxygen resistance of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr without degrading its intrinsic mechanical properties.
generation.material_initial_state: Cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr exhibiting 8–16% room‑temperature tensile ductility and yield strengths of 163–530 MPa at 1000 °C, but with poor oxygen resistance.
generation.intervention: Apply a thin aluminide coating (or equivalent alumina‐forming coating) on the surface of the alloy using a controlled deposition process.
generation.conditions: High-temperature exposure at approximately 1000 °C in air for durations on the order of hours, under strain rates of 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹ during mechanical testing.
generation.structural_mediator: A continuous, stable Al₂O₃ (alumina) scale formed by the coating that serves as a diffusion barrier to oxygen.
generation.mechanism: The aluminide coating undergoes oxidation to form a protective alumina layer that limits further oxygen ingress, preserving the alloy’s bulk microstructure and maintaining its mechanical performance.
generation.predicted_outcome: The coated alloy will show significantly reduced oxidation (lower weight gain and minimal oxide scale growth) under high-temperature air exposure relative to the untreated alloy while retaining similar tensile ductility and yield strength.
generation.baseline: Untreated cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr, which suffers from rapid oxidation under similar high-temperature air exposure conditions.
generation.boundary: The intervention is effective during short-to-moderate high-temperature exposures (~1000 °C, air atmosphere, a few hours) and under mechanical loading regimes similar to those tested in prior studies (strain rates 10⁻⁴–10⁻² s⁻¹).
generation.uncertainty: The optimum coating thickness, deposition parameters, and long-term stability of the alumina scale under cyclic thermal and mechanical loads require further investigation.

falsification_experiment.design: Prepare two groups of samples: one group of cast equiatomic HfNbTaTiZr with the applied aluminide coating and an uncoated control group. Subject both groups to isothermal oxidation at 1000 °C in air for a fixed duration (e.g., 5 hours) followed by mechanical testing at room temperature and at 1000 °C.
measurements: Weight gain and oxide scale thickness (via gravimetric analysis and microscopy)
Surface oxide scale composition (using SEM/EDS or XRD)
High-temperature yield strength (via tensile or compressive tests)
falsification_experiment.falsification_rule: If the aluminide-coated samples do not show a statistically significant improvement in oxidation resistance compared to the uncoated controls, or if the mechanical properties (tensile ductility or yield strength) are notably degraded after coating and exposure, then the hypothesis is falsified.

cited_evidence.text:
Effects of Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr on Mechanical Properties of Equiatomic Hf-Mo-Nb-Ta-Ti-Zr Alloys

Abstract: AbstractNowadays refractory high-entropy alloys (RHEAs) are regarded as great candidates for the replacement of superalloys at high temperature. To design a RHEA, one must understand the pros and cons of every refractory element. However, the elemental effect on mechanical properties remains unclear. In this study, the subtraction method was applied on equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys to discover the role of each element, and, thus, HfMoNbTaTiZr, HfNbTaTiZr, HfMoTaTiZr, HfMoNbTiZr, HfMoNbTaZr, and HfMoNbTaTi were fabricated and analyzed. The microstructure and mechanical properties of each alloy at the as-cast state were examined. The solid solution phase formation rule and the solution strengthening effect are also discussed. Finally, the mechanism of how Mo, Nb, Ta, Ti, and Zr affect the HfMoNbTaTiZr alloys was established after comparing the properties of these alloys.Keywords: high-entropy alloys, refractory high-entropy alloys, alloys design, elevated-temperature yield strength, solid solution strengthening effect

Conclusions: The equiatomic HfMoNbTaTiZr alloy was chosen
